name: Rigging and Restraint Readiness Verification
description: Before the drop run, the Loadmaster verifies that CDS bundle rigging and restraint meets standard before the aircraft can proceed to release.
criteria: CDS bundle rigging and restraint configuration meets DAFMAN 13-217 drop-zone/airdrop standards.
possibleOutcomes: Not ready — delay or correct rigging before proceeding

name: Release Execution
description: The Loadmaster's hand is on the release mechanism during the drop run; physical release is executed only on the Aircraft Commander's verbal command, confirmed by a flight-deck signal that cargo is ready and the drop zone is clear.
criteria: Release is executed only after the Aircraft Commander's verbal 'Mark' command, confirmed by a flight-deck 'cargo ready / drop zone clear' signal — never on the Loadmaster's unilateral initiative.
possibleOutcomes: Release executed, confirmed to flight deck ("Cargo away")

doctrineSource.publication: C-17 Pilot (c17pilot.com), "C-17 Airdrop Operations — How Cargo and Troops Exit at 25,000 Feet"
doctrineSource.note: NOT an official Air Force publication — an enthusiast/educational site. Cited for the specific call-and-response procedure (pilot 'Mark' → Loadmaster 'Cargo away', green-light flight-deck signal) because no official source for this exact sequence was independently accessible this session (every .mil domain network-blocked). The general framework — CDS release under aircrew/DZ coordination — is grounded in DAFMAN 13-217; this specific verbal-procedure detail is not verified against a primary Air Force source and should be treated as illustrative/representative rather than doctrinally confirmed.

name: In-Flight Malfunction / Abort Call
description: During the drop run-in, the Loadmaster monitors the cargo compartment and rigging for equipment failures and can call for the release to be aborted.
criteria: Any detected equipment malfunction or rigging failure that would compromise a safe release.
possibleOutcomes: Call abort and report the malfunction to the Aircraft Commander

name: UAV Pallet Configuration Verification Against TOC-L Flight Plan
description: Before the drop run, the Loadmaster verifies that the Rapid Dragon-class pallet configuration and UAV launch sequence match the flight plan and launch instructions provided by the TOC-L Coordinator.
criteria: Pallet configuration, UAV launch sequence, and release parameters match the TOC-L-provided flight plan exactly.
possibleOutcomes: Configuration verified — proceed with launch sequence
Discrepancy identified — hold and coordinate with TOC-L before release

doctrineSource.publication: Air Force Research Laboratory, "Rapid Dragon" / "Palletized Effects"
doctrineSource.note: General Rapid Dragon-class pallet concept confirmed (see rapid-dragon-palletized-effects-system System record). The specific loadmaster verification procedure against a TOC-L-produced flight plan is not documented in any source found this session — this Decision is a reasonable structural inference (a loadmaster verifying configuration against instructions before release is standard practice for any pre-release check, per the existing loadmaster-rigging-readiness-verification Decision) applied to this mission's new payload type, not a directly documented procedure.

name: In-Flight Patient Status Decision
description: During flight, the Flight Nurse (Medical Crew Director) assesses whether a patient's condition remains within the bounds anticipated by their assigned precedence category (Urgent/Urgent-Surg/Priority/Routine/Convenience) and takes action if it does not — including advising the Aircraft Commander of a need affecting flight operations.
criteria: Patient vital signs and condition, as reported by the AE Technician and shown on patient monitoring equipment, measured against the patient's assigned precedence category and expected in-flight course.
possibleOutcomes: Provide in-flight intervention within AECM scope of care
Advise Aircraft Commander of a flight-operations need (e.g. altitude restriction) or, in the most severe case, request diversion

doctrineSource.publication: AFI 48-307 / DAFI 48-107 series; NATO AAMedP-1.1/1.5 (STANAG 3204/2087) for the precedence taxonomy
doctrineSource.note: The Medical Crew Director's overall supervisory/decision authority for in-flight patient care is confirmed (same sourcing as the flight-nurse-medical-crew-director Role record). The precedence-category taxonomy (Urgent/Urgent-Surg/Priority/Routine/Convenience) is NATO-sourced (same sourcing as the tpmrc C2Node record) rather than a directly fetched USAF-specific enumeration; the specific decision structure and outcome set here are this dataset's reasonable structuring of that authority, not a quoted procedure.

name: Patient Manifest Verification Against TPMRC-Validated PMR
description: Before departure, the Flight Nurse (Medical Crew Director) verifies that the actual patient load — count, precedence mix, and litter/ambulatory breakdown — matches the TPMRC-validated Patient Movement Request, the AE mission's analogue to the Loadmaster's pre-release rigging/configuration checks in Missions 1-2.
criteria: Patient count, precedence mix, and litter/ambulatory breakdown match the TPMRC-validated PMR exactly.
possibleOutcomes: Discrepancy identified — hold and coordinate with TPMRC before departure

doctrineSource.publication: USTRANSCOM patient movement doctrine (via web search synthesis)
doctrineSource.note: Same verification status as the tpmrc C2Node record's citation. The general PMR validation process is confirmed; the specific pre-departure MCD verification step modeled here is a reasonable structural inference (a pre-release/pre-departure verification against validated instructions is standard practice, per the existing loadmaster-rigging-readiness-verification and loadmaster-uav-pallet-configuration-verification Decisions), not a directly documented procedure.

name: Weather Go/No-Go and Divert Decision
description: Before departure and continuously during the mission, the Aircraft Commander assesses current and forecast weather — starting with the pre-flight Flight Weather Briefing (DD Form 175-1) and updated by the in-flight weather data stream — against aircraft and mission-specific weather minimums, and decides whether to proceed, delay, or divert.
criteria: Observed and forecast weather (ceiling, visibility, winds, icing, thunderstorm activity) at departure, en route, and destination/drop-zone, measured against aircraft and mission-specific weather minimums.
possibleOutcomes: Divert to an alternate or abort the mission leg

doctrineSource.publication: DD Form 175-1, "Flight Weather Briefing"; AFDP 3-59, Weather Operations
doctrineSource.note: The weather-minimums go/no-go decision is standard aviation practice, confirmed generically via web search on 2026-09-10; DD Form 175-1's structure (mission/takeoff data, en-route data, terminal forecast, hazards including turbulence/icing/thunderstorms) is confirmed as the standard USAF pre-flight weather-briefing input to exactly this kind of decision. The specific outcome set and continuous (not just pre-flight) framing here is this dataset's reasonable structuring of that authority, not a quoted procedure.
